sections.notes: Section frame ('Hero FB' / 'hero Fb', 1366x553 incl. 12px side padding) has an image-fill background: get_design_context on it (and on the mobile 'Hero' node) returns ONE flattened PNG with all text/UI baked in, even though the underlying Figma layers (title, description, select input, map, detail card) are real separate nodes with real colours/text obtainable via get_design_context on each sub-node directly. Both desktop and mobile images were downloaded as raw/hero-fb-background-{desktop,mobile}.png. Gradient (sampled with ImageMagick from the exported PNGs, not a flat colour): primarily top-to-bottom, roughly linear-gradient(180deg, #c33d33 0%, #f6e6cf 100%), warmer/pinker at top-right (~#ee9c93) than top-left on desktop; same red->cream direction on mobile (~#d53a3c top to ~#f6e6cf bottom). Corner radius: 20px desktop, 52px mobile. Card: bg #ffffff, radius 16px, 24px padding, 16px gap between the 4 detail rows, 1px #ececec dividers between rows (visible in rendered image). Detail row icon box: 40x40, radius 8px, bg #eeeeee, border 1px #dedede, icon 20x20 centered. Label text (Address/Phone/Branch Timing/Write to us on) is #808080 12px/18px Manrope semibold; value text is #121212 12px/18px Manrope semibold, except the 'Toll-Free:' label+number which is #0a8452 (green) with the number underlined. Select City control is the shared '🌐 Breakpoint_Input field' component (label 'Select City', value 'Agra', chevron-down icon) — checked includeHidden:true on the instance (desktop node 5082:46404) and found only generic hidden component-state children (icon variants, keyboard-type variants, helper text) that belong to the shared component, not additional city options or hidden city panels; also re-checked includeHidden on the parent 'hero Fb' tree (5082:46396) and found no hidden siblings for other cities. So this page only has Agra authored; other cities are presumably populated at runtime, not present in Figma. Desktop layout: title+description full width at top, then a row with select+map stacked on the left (587px) and the address/phone/timing/email card on the right (583px). Mobile layout differs in stacking order: title, description, select input, THEN the detail card, THEN the map image at the very bottom (card is above the map on mobile, left-of/beside it on desktop).
